nice-finerenone-chronic-heart-failure.name: NICE backs finerenone for heart failure
nice-finerenone-chronic-heart-failure.headline: NICE final draft guidance recommends finerenone for chronic heart failure
nice-finerenone-chronic-heart-failure.summary: NICE final draft guidance recommends finerenone for adults with chronic heart failure with preserved or mildly reduced ejection fraction.
keyPoints: NICE has published final draft guidance that recommends finerenone for adults with chronic heart failure with preserved or mildly reduced ejection fraction.
NICE estimates that up to 280,000 people in England could be eligible for finerenone.
NICE says about half of the estimated 635,000 people in England with heart failure have preserved or mildly reduced ejection fraction.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body: NICE has published final draft guidance that recommends finerenone for adults with chronic heart failure that has preserved or mildly reduced ejection fraction. Finerenone belongs to a group of medicines called mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists. NICE estimates that up to 280,000 people could be eligible for it.

body.heading: What it means
body.body: NICE says that of the estimated 635,000 people in England who have heart failure, about half have preserved or mildly reduced ejection fraction. The announcement also reports around 100,000 hospital admissions for heart failure in England in 2023 to 2024. NICE recommended dapagliflozin in 2023 for the same group of people, and it was the first NICE-recommended treatment for this type of heart failure. Final draft guidance is the stage before NICE publishes its final guidance.

source.title: Thousands eligible for new chronic heart failure treatment following NICE recommendation

nice-endometriosis-tests-primary-care.name: NICE: endometriosis tests in primary care
nice-endometriosis-tests-primary-care.headline: NICE draft guidance proposes two non-invasive endometriosis tests for NHS primary care
nice-endometriosis-tests-primary-care.summary: NICE draft guidance proposes that two non-invasive tests for endometriosis could be used in NHS primary care while more evidence is gathered.
keyPoints: NICE draft guidance proposes that two non-invasive diagnostic tests for endometriosis could be used in NHS primary care while more evidence on their accuracy is gathered.
The two tests are Endotest, which analyses a saliva sample, and EndoSure, which measures electrical signals in the gut.
NICE says the average wait for an endometriosis diagnosis is more than nine years.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body: NICE has published draft guidance proposing that two non-invasive diagnostic tests for endometriosis could be used in the NHS in primary care while more evidence on their accuracy is gathered. Endotest analyses a saliva sample for tiny biological markers called microRNAs. EndoSure detects endometriosis by measuring electrical signals in the gut.

body.heading: What it means
body.body: NICE says the average wait for an endometriosis diagnosis is more than nine years. A third test, DotEndo, which is a blood test, is not among the tests in the draft recommendations. Because this is draft guidance, the recommendations may change after consultation.

source.title: New technologies could help cut years-long wait for endometriosis diagnosis, says NICE

nice-pmos-draft-guideline.name: NICE draft guideline renames PCOS as PMOS
nice-pmos-draft-guideline.headline: NICE draft guideline on PMOS recommends a yearly check and quicker diagnosis
nice-pmos-draft-guideline.summary: NICE has published a draft guideline on polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), formerly called PCOS, for public consultation.
keyPoints: The draft guideline was open for feedback from 1 July to 11 August 2026.
NICE says people with PMOS should be offered a yearly check covering symptoms, treatment and long-term health risks.
NICE says the draft aims for diagnosis to happen sooner.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body: NICE has published a draft guideline on polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), the condition formerly called polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), for public consultation. The draft was open for feedback from healthcare professionals, patients and the public from 1 July to 11 August 2026. It adapts the 2023 international guideline on PCOS to UK practice.

body.heading: What it means
body.body: NICE says people with PMOS should be offered a yearly check covering symptoms, treatment and long-term health risks, and that diagnosis should happen sooner. The draft sets out detailed guidance on when to suspect the condition, and says PMOS should not be ruled out after menopause.

source.title: New draft PMOS guideline recommends annual review and could mean quicker diagnosis

references.title: New draft PMOS guideline recommends annual review and could mean quicker diagnosis

nice-osteoporosis-risk-assessment-guidel.name: NICE publishes osteoporosis risk guideline
nice-osteoporosis-risk-assessment-guidel.headline: NICE publishes new guideline on assessing fracture risk in adults
nice-osteoporosis-risk-assessment-guidel.summary: NICE published guideline NG259 on 29 July 2026, covering how adults at risk of fragility fractures should be assessed. It replaces an earlier guideline.
keyPoints: NICE published its osteoporosis risk assessment guideline, NG259, on 29 July 2026.
NG259 replaces the earlier guideline CG146 and is the first part of a wider update.
The second part, on treatment and monitoring, is still in development.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body: NICE published a new guideline, Osteoporosis: risk assessment (NG259), on 29 July 2026. It replaces guideline CG146 and is the first part of a wider update. NICE says it covers fragility fracture risk assessment, identifying vertebral fragility fractures, deciding whether drug treatment is appropriate, and follow-up for people not having treatment.

body.heading: What it means
body.body: The second part of the update, on treatment and monitoring, is still in development. A fragility fracture is a broken bone caused by a fall from standing height or less.

nice-weekly-insulin-efsitora.name: NICE backs weekly insulin for type 2 diabetes
nice-weekly-insulin-efsitora.headline: NICE final draft guidance recommends once-weekly insulin efsitora alfa for type 2 diabetes
nice-weekly-insulin-efsitora.summary: NICE has recommended a once-a-week insulin, insulin efsitora alfa (Onswik), for adults with type 2 diabetes in final draft guidance.
keyPoints: NICE recommended a once-a-week insulin for adults with type 2 diabetes in a news release dated 20 August 2026.
NICE says it needs one injection a week, which could cut injections from 365 a year to 52.
NICE says it works about as well as insulins already used for type 2 diabetes.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body: NICE has recommended insulin efsitora alfa, sold as Onswik and made by Eli Lilly, for adults with type 2 diabetes. This was final draft guidance. It is injected once a week, and NICE says this could cut injections from 365 a year to 52. NICE says it gives blood glucose control similar to people's current treatment, and can be used alone or alongside other treatments.

body.heading: What it means
body.body: NICE expects the biggest benefit for people who need a carer or family member to help with injections, and for those with extra care needs. The draft says the medicine must be licensed by the MHRA before it can be made available on the NHS. It also says healthcare professionals and patients should discuss the options and choose the least expensive treatment that meets the person's needs. NICE's guidance page for the appraisal (TA1200) lists final guidance as published on 16 October 2026.

source.title: Weekly insulin jab could cut injections from 365 a year to just 52

nice-type-2-diabetes-appraisals-update.name: NICE aligns type 2 diabetes drug guidance
nice-type-2-diabetes-appraisals-update.headline: NICE updates four type 2 diabetes appraisals and withdraws four dapagliflozin appraisals
nice-type-2-diabetes-appraisals-update.summary: NICE has updated four technology appraisals on type 2 diabetes medicines to match its type 2 diabetes guideline, and withdrawn four on dapagliflozin.
keyPoints: On 15 September 2026 NICE published a news story on updating four technology appraisals for type 2 diabetes.
The updated appraisals were brought into line with NICE's guideline on type 2 diabetes in adults.
NICE describes the exercise as the first test of a new way of keeping all of its guidance aligned.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body: NICE has updated four technology appraisals for type 2 diabetes medicines so that they match the recommendations in its guideline on type 2 diabetes in adults. NICE says the pilot shows that appraisals can be kept aligned with guidelines more efficiently, without compromising the rigour or transparency of its decisions.

body.heading: What it means
body.body: NICE also withdrew four appraisals on dapagliflozin: TA288, TA390, TA418 and TA583. It treats the withdrawal as a routing decision, and says it is not subject to appeal. NICE describes the exercise as the first test of a new way of keeping all of its guidance aligned.

source.title: Faster alignment of technology appraisals with clinical guidelines trialled in type 2 diabetes update

references.title: Faster alignment of technology appraisals with clinical guidelines trialled in type 2 diabetes update

nice-ai-prostate-mri.name: NICE: AI tools for prostate MRI scans
nice-ai-prostate-mri.headline: NICE draft guidance backs five AI tools to help read prostate MRI scans
nice-ai-prostate-mri.summary: NICE draft guidance recommends five AI tools as NHS options to help radiologists spot prostate cancer on MRI scans.
keyPoints: NICE announced on 23 October 2026 that five AI technologies are recommended in draft guidance for NHS use to help detect prostate cancer on MRI scans.
The tools highlight areas on a scan where cancer might be present, to help radiologists spot and report it.
NICE says comments from the consultation will be considered by the independent committee before final guidance is published.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body: NICE draft guidance recommends that five AI technologies can be used in the NHS as options to help detect prostate cancer on MRI scans while further evidence is generated. The tools highlight areas on a prostate MRI scan where cancer might be present, which NICE says makes it easier for radiologists to spot and report. Comments received during the consultation will be considered by the independent committee before final guidance is published.

body.heading: What it means
body.body: NICE says the tools could help radiologists identify clinically significant prostate cancer more accurately and consistently, while helping NHS services manage growing demand for scans.

source.title: New AI tools could help spot prostate cancer more accurately

references.title: New AI tools could help spot prostate cancer more accurately
